transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-10
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Jamal Ortiz (Redwood SE), Sara Li (Nimbus Head of ML), Tom Brenner (CTO), Priya Kaur (Procurement)

[00:00:00] Lena: Hi everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intro from Redwood side, I'm Lena, AE, and Jamal is our SE.
[00:00:10] Jamal: Hey hi, afternoon all. We'll try to keep it practical — want to align on success criteria and what you need to see in the pilot.
[00:00:20] Sara: Thanks. We have a pretty tight timeline Q1 launch, so pilot needs to prove latency and cost. I can share current traffic patterns.
[00:00:35] Tom: Yes, objective is to replace our current in-house numpy-model endoint — looking at inference economics more than model novelty.
[00:00:45] Lena: Great, can you summarize concrete KPIs you care about? Jamal, maybe follow on throughput needs.
[00:00:55] Sara: Sure — p95 latency target: under 500ms for typical 512-token responses. Throughput: support ~150 concurrent active users, which maps to roughly 2.5k tokens/sec sustained during peaks. Quality: less than 5% delta on our core NPS metric vs baseline. Cost: we'd like to understand cost per 1M tokens and projected monthly run rate.
[00:01:20] Jamal: That's helpful. For sizing we'll ask for a sample token distribution and some representative prompt sets. We usually size GPU pools around peak tokens/sec and KV cache hit rates.
[00:01:40] Sara: We'll get logs — note some token spikes when long context searches happen.
[00:01:50] Priya: On procurement, small pilots under $25k go via PO. Anything larger requires SOW/contract, which will extend timeline. We prefer a 30-day pilot if possible.
[00:02:05] Lena: Good to know — Redwood typically offers pilot credits and a simple pilot term sheet. Jamal, can you talk about the commercial guardrails we recommend?
[00:02:18] Jamal: Sure. For a 30-day POC we typically provide credits mapped to expected throughput and buffer for testing — two common structures: 1) Fixed credit pool (e.g., 50-100k tokens equivalent per day) or 2) Metered credits with spend cap. We also put caps on peak QPS to protect other customers, but for Dedicated we can carve capacity.
[00:02:45] Tom: Can you convert that to dollars? Our CFO will want a sense of runway.
[00:02:53] Lena: We'll send a simple spreadsheet: estimated credits, what they map to in token usage, and an illustrative dollar conversion using hosted vs dedicated pricing. As a rough order, small pilot starting credits often are in the $10-30k equivalent range depending on throughput.
[00:03:12] Sara: Important — we need canonical benchmark numbers: p50/p95 latency, throughput, and cost per 1M tokens. Also, any variance between hosted vs dedicated and the possibility of Redwood Private with VPC later.
[00:03:30] Jamal: We'll run two bench types: a smoke benchmark to validate latency SLOs with your prompt set, and a soak test to validate throughput and cache behavior. For hosted we can iterate quickly; Dedicated gives more predictable throughput and tail latency. Private (VPC) usually comes later.
[00:03:50] Speaker 1: (mumbled) and the quantization options?
[00:03:55] Jamal: Right — quantization and model variant selection impact both latency and cost. We'll propose a baseline model configuration (float16 or 8-bit quant) as part of the benchmark plan. Sometimes the name of the model gets garbled in transcription — but we'll pick a Redwood-verified variant that matches your quality.
[00:04:14] Sara: For success criteria — we want: p95 <500ms, throughput to handle 2.5k tokens/sec at peak, plus <5% quality drift. If we hit those, procurement will move to pilot sign-off.
[00:04:30] Lena: Sounds reasonable. On the commercial guardrails side: pilot length 30 days, credit cap to limit spend, and explicit acceptance criteria that if met we proceed to contracting. If acceptance met and spend expectation >25k, procurement will go SOW.
[00:04:50] Tom: Is there an auto-fallover if spikes exceed credits? We don't want production risk.
[00:04:56] Jamal: We can enable hard caps on consumption or soft alerts and automatic fallback to a cheaper model (or rate-limiting). During the pilot we usually recommend setting hard spend caps to stop runaway costs.
[00:05:10] Priya: Also need SOC2 and encryption details before any PII leaves our environment. Is that in the pack you mentioned?
[00:05:18] Lena: Yes, we'll share the security pack — SOC 2 Type II attestation, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integrations, and audit logs in the Console.
[00:05:30] Jamal: For benchmarks we'll ask for an anonymized sample of request/response traces, token histograms, and a list of failure cases you care about. That lets us simulate prefix caching and KV hits.
[00:05:45] Sara: How long does the setup take? We run in AWS; if it's hosted it's quick, Dedicated might take 1-2 weeks to provision.
[00:05:54] Jamal: Hosted — we can start benching within 48-72 hours once we have sample prompts and an API key. Dedicated provisioning depends on capacity; for pilot reservations often 7-10 business days. Private deployment adds more time for networking.
[00:06:10] Lena: OK, high level timeline: 2–3 days to get initial benchmarks, week to iterate, pilot runs for 30 days. Procurement touchpoints at pilot start and before any transition to SOW.
[00:06:22] Tom: Regarding metrics — can we get per-route latency and token-level cost breakdown in the Console?
[00:06:28] Jamal: Yes, Console shows per-route cost, token-level breakdown, and you can tag routes for team chargebacks. We'll include a sample dashboard.
[00:06:40] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) also what about model rollbacks?
[00:06:44] Jamal: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies; that helps limit regressions during the pilot if we adjust model variants.
[00:06:55] Sara: For the benchmark plan, please include: test harness, traffic replay, cold vs warm KV cache scenarios, and quantized vs full-precision runs.
[00:07:06] Jamal: Noted — we'll include those dimensions. We'll also propose acceptance thresholds and measurement windows (e.g., 24h rolling for latency).
[00:07:18] Lena: Quick commercial items: pilot credits, invoice vs credit usage, and what happens if we exceed credits.
[00:07:25] Priya: For PO path — if pilot cap <= $25k we can issue PO. If it's greater, we need legal SOW. Also need Redwood's standard T&Cs and any data processing addendum.
[00:07:38] Lena: We'll include a short term sheet and the DPA. For pilot overspend the default is to suspend until a PO is in place unless you agree to auto-bill. We usually avoid auto-bill for first pilots.
[00:07:54] Tom: Can you provide a sample SOW template? Contracts team needs to see it.
[00:07:58] Lena: Yes, we'll share the SOW template.
[00:08:05] Sara: A couple of edge questions — do you do evaluation metrics for hallucination/regression? We have a labeled set to check.
[00:08:13] Jamal: We can run rouge/bleu-like or custom metrics; plus Redwood Optimize has eval hooks to run regressions against baseline prompts. We'll propose an eval suite.
[00:08:27] Speaker 1: (inaudible) what about multi-region?
[00:08:30] Jamal: We can route by region; for pilot we'll focus on the primary region but can test cross-region fallbacks.
[00:08:40] Lena: Alright, let's recap and assign owners — Jamal will draft the benchmark plan and tell us what traces he needs. Lena will send credits spreadsheet and term sheet. Sara will share prompt set. Priya will outline procurement constraints.
[00:08:58] Tom: Sounds good. Also please include an estimated conversion path to Dedicated (lead time, costs) if we want to move to reserved capacity after pilot.
[00:09:08] Jamal: We'll include a conversion playbook: performance profile, projected monthly tokens, and typical commit tiers.
[00:09:16] Sara: Any immediate blockers?
[00:09:18] Priya: Only if the pilot credit value is above our PO threshold. Otherwise legal review of DPA/SOW is standard.
[00:09:26] Lena: We'll aim to keep pilot under PO threshold unless you opt-in to larger run.
[00:09:32] Jamal: One more note — during benching if we see tokenization mismatches we'll flag prompt engineering changes; that can change throughput/cost.
[00:09:44] Sara: Okay. When can we expect the benchmark plan?
[00:09:47] Jamal: I'll send a draft within 3 business days after this call.
[00:09:52] Lena: I'll send the credit spreadsheet and term sheet in 48 hours.
[00:09:56] Priya: I'll aim to respond with procurement constraints within a week.
[00:10:02] Lena: Great. Any final questions?
[00:10:05] Tom: No, thanks.
[00:10:07] Sara: Thanks everyone.
[00:10:10] Lena: Thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark workshop.
[00:10:15] Jamal: Thanks, bye.

Transcript notes:
- Occasional mis-transcriptions of product names (e.g., "Redwood Console" rendered as "red wood console") and acronyms.
- Natural speech patterns: pauses, fillers, and slight crosstalk.
- Recording ended at ~15:55 UTC.

End of transcript.
